 Ruben Amorim's AC Milan visit Genoa at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris in the 11th round of Serie A. They arrive at Marassi still downcast after a heavy home defeat to Ferencvaros in the Europa League, which has tempered the enthusiasm generated by their Derby della Madonnina victory.
 Meanwhile, Daniele De Rossi's Genoa are in excellent form. They've won their last three league matches, including a notable home victory over Juventus, and go into this one with renewed confidence.
 Fifth in Serie A, AC Milan remain well placed in the table, but their inconsistent performances are a concern. Amorim has an injury-depleted squad, particularly in defence, and faces growing questions about the group's mental resilience after their European disappointments.
 Diego Moreira, a standout performer in the derby with a goal and two assists, will be looking to deliver away from home too. The Portuguese talent is one of AC Milan's few reasons for optimism, alongside Gonçalo Ramos, who is seeking consistency in front of goal.
 In 12th, Genoa are showing signs of improvement and have proved capable of beating higher-ranked opponents. De Rossi has found balance and identity in his side, and the Ferraris promises to be a difficult place to visit.

 Daniele De Rossi's Genoa will be without Elias Havel, Lorenzo Venturino and Joi Xheto Nuredini through injury. Bijlow is likely to start in goal behind a back three of Marcandalli, Oestigard and Vasquez, with El Shaarawy and Baldanzi supporting Osmajic.
 At AC Milan, Amorim faces a defensive injury crisis: Saelemaekers, Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Terracciano, Chukwueze, Pavlovic and Tomori are all out injured. Maignan is likely to start in goal, with De Winter, Gila and Diawara in defence, Estupinan at left-back, and Moreira, Ramos and Pulisic in attack with Modric directing play.

They beat Lecce 2-1 in their most recent league match, having previously beaten Juventus 2-0 at home. Across those five games, De Rossi's side have scored six goals and conceded five.
 By contrast, AC Milan have two wins, no draws and three defeats in their last five matches across Serie A and the Europa League. A 2-0 defeat to Ferencvaros followed their 3-1 derby win over Inter. They've scored six goals and conceded nine in that period, underlining their defensive difficulties.
